36829.subject: Chemistry
36829.question_text: Elements which belong to the same group in the Periodic Table are characterized by
36829.explanation: Elements in the same group have the same number of valence electron in their outermost shell while elements in the same period have the same number of shells.

options.text: difference of +1 in the oxidation numbers of successive members
presence of the same number of outermost electrons in the respective atoms
difference of 14 atomic mass units between successive members

36830.subject: Chemistry
36830.question_text: The atom of an element X combines with aluminium (\(_{13}\)AI). What is the formula of the compound formed?
36830.explanation: Even though we were not told if the element X were a monoatomic or diatomic, inasmuch as Aluminium has a valency of +3, and there is going to be an exchange of valency between the two atoms of elements combining, X will definitely take the 3 from Al, and from the options, only option D has X having 3. Consequently, the correct option is D.

36831.subject: Chemistry
36831.question_text: The presence of unpaired electrons in an atom of a transition metal gives rise to
36831.explanation: Paramagnetism occurs when an atom or material has unpaired electrons, which act like tiny magnets due to their spin. The magnetic moment of an electron is a result of its spin and orbital motion. Paramagnetism in transition metals is caused by the presence of unpaired electrons in their atomic and ionic species.

36832.subject: Chemistry
36832.explanation: The positive ions and delocalized electrons are strongly attracted to each other, forming a metallic bond. Metallic bonding occurs when positively charged metal ions are attracted to delocalized electrons.

options.text: Sharing of electrons between the metal atoms
Attraction between the atomic unclei and cloud of electrons
transfer of electrons from one atom to another
Attraction between positive and negative ions

36833.subject: Chemistry
36833.question_text: Which of the following compounds is covalent?
36833.explanation: A covalent compound is a molecule that is formed when two or more different atoms are connected with a covalent bond. Covalent compounds are basically the molecules that form when two different atoms form a covalent bond. They typically have similar electronegativity and are non-metals. Only Option D has two non-metals.

36834.subject: Chemistry
36834.question_text: A sheet of paper is placed in the path of a beam from a radioactive source. The emissions that pass through the paper consist of
36834.explanation: Among the three types of radiations, alpha, beta and Gamma rays, it is only alpha rays that cannot penetrate a piece of paper or human hand, as it has the lowest penetrating power though the highest ionizing power. However, Beta particles and Gamma rays can pass through or penetrate a piece of paper. Option C is the correct answer.

36836.subject: Chemistry
36836.question_text: Which of the following features of a human skeleton can be determined by carbon-dating?
36836.explanation: Radiocarbon dating is often used in forensics to determine the age and year of death of unidentified human remains. It can also be used to identify a person's year of birth by measuring carbon-14 levels in tooth enamel. Carbon-dating, also known as carbon-14 dating, can be used to determine the age of a human skeleton.

36839.subject: Chemistry
36839.question_text: Which of the following statements about ideal gases is/are correct? 1. The cohesive forces between their particles are negligible ll. They have no definite volume but occupy the volume of their containers III. They are not compressible IV. Their particles collide with loss of energy
36839.explanation:
Here are some  properties of ideal gases:

  • Inert: Ideal gases are assumed to not react with each other.
  • Elastic collisions: Ideal gases collide with the container's walls elastically, meaning they don't lose energy after collisions. 
  • Take the shape of their container: Ideal gases take the shape of their container, so the volume of the container is the same as the volume of the gas.
  • Follow the ideal gas law: The ideal gas law is PV= nRT
  • Compressibility factor of 1: The compressibility factor of an ideal gas is exactly 1.

36840.subject: Chemistry
36840.question_text: P\(_{TOTAL}\) = P\(_1\) + P\(_2\) + P\(_3\) + ...Pn' where P Total is the pressure of a mixture of gasses. The equation above is an expression of
36840.explanation: Dalton’s Law, or the Law of Partial Pressures, states that the total pressure exerted by a mixture of gases is equal to the sum of the partial pressures of the gases in the mixture.  P\(_T\) = P\(_1\) + P\(_2\) + P\(_3\) + ...

36841.subject: Chemistry
36841.question_text: Which of the following pairs of reagents react to produce hydrogen?
36841.explanation:
When magnesium reacts with dilute sulfuric acid, it produces magnesium sulfate and hydrogen gas.

The chemical equation for this reaction is:

                      Mg(s) + H2SO4(aq) → MgSO4(aq) +  H2(g)

36842.subject: Chemistry
36842.question_text: A mixture of calcium chloride and calcium trioxocarbonate (IV) in water can be separated by
36842.explanation:
To separate calcium chloride (CaCl2) and calcium carbonate (CaCO3) in water, you can add water to the mixture, filter it, and collect the CaCO3 on the filter paper.

The CaCl2 solution will pass through the filter paper, while the CaCO3 will be collected on the paper. This is possible because CaCO3 is insoluble in water, while CaCl2 is soluble. The correct answer is option D

36843.subject: Chemistry
36843.question_text: Which of the following would dissolve in warm dilute H2SO4 without effervescence, to give a blue solution?
36843.explanation:
Copper turnings will dissolve in warm dilute sulfuric acid (H2SO4) without effervescence to give a blue solution.

When copper reacts with sulfuric acid, it forms copper sulfate (CuSO4), a salt that is blue in color. The reaction is: 

  • Cu (s) + H2SO4 (aq) → CuSO4 (aq) + H2 (g) ↑ 
  • Copper + Sulfuric acid → Copper sulfate + Hydrogen

36845.subject: Chemistry
36845.question_text: In which of the reactions represented by the following equations is HNO3 behaving as a typical acid?
36845.explanation: When an acid (HNO3) reacts with a base(CaO), the products are usually salts( Ca(NO3)2 and water(H2O). Hence, HNO3 behaved like a typical acid in Option A.

36846.subject: Chemistry
36846.question_text: A gas was evolved when a sample of gastric juice reacted with sodium trioxocarbonate (IV) . The gas evolved was
36846.explanation: Gastric juice is made up of hydrochloric acid, digestive enzymes, and other substances that help absorb nutrients. However, whenever a carbonate(IV) salt reacts with an acid (HCl), CO\(_2\) is evolved.

36847.subject: Chemistry
36847.question_text: It can be concluded that gastric juice
36847.explanation: Gastric juice is made up of hydrochloric acid, digestive enzymes, and other substances that help absorb nutrients. It is highly acidic.

36848.explanation:
Electron affinity is defined as the amount of energy released when an electron is added to a neutral atom to form an anion. 

From the reaction, an electron is added to a neutral atom, Cl, and an anion Cl- is formed. Therefore, the correct answer is option B

36851.subject: Chemistry
36851.question_text: A reaction is represented by the equation below. A2(g) + B2(g)  → 2AB(g); ∆H = +X kJmol-1 Which of the following statements about the system is correct?

At equilibrium increase in temperature favours the reverse reaction

36852.subject: Chemistry
36852.question_text: What is the oxidation number of nitrogen in Al(NO\(_3\))\(_3\)?
36852.explanation:
The oxidation number of Al = +3 , O = - 2, N =?  in Al(NO\(_3\) )\(_3\)

                            Al(NO\(_3\) )\(_3\) = 0

                            Al + 3N + 3(O3) = 0

                            +3 + 3N + 3(-2 X 3) = 0

36853.subject: Chemistry
36853.question_text: What is oxidized in the reaction represented by the following equation? 3CU + 8HNO3 → 3Cu(NO3)2 + 2NO + 4H2O
36853.explanation: Copper is oxidized because there is an increase of oxidation number from 0 (LHS) to +2 (RHS).

36855.subject: Chemistry
36855.question_text: Which of the following substances decomposes when an electric current is passed through it?
36855.explanation: Glucose does not decompose when an electric current passes through it because it is a non-electrolyte and does not conduct electricity. However, hydrochloric acid (HCl) does decompose when an electric current passes through it because it is a strong electrolyte.

36856.subject: Chemistry
36856.question_text: A concentrated solution containing H+, Cu2+,OH- and CI- was electrolyzed using platinum electrodes which of the ions will be discharged at the cathode?
36856.explanation:
When using a platinum electrode, copper ions (Cu2+) are deposited at the cathode, while hydrogen ions (H+) remain in solution.

Here's what happens during the electrolysis of a copper sulfate solution using a platinum cathode:

  • Cathode: Copper ions are attracted to the negative cathode and are deposited as a reddish layer of pure copper 
  • Anode: Oxygen gas is liberated 
  • Electrolyte: The blue color of the electrolyte disappears and it becomes dilute sulfuric acid.    The less reactive a metal, the more readily its ion is reduced on the electrode surface.

36859.subject: Chemistry
36859.question_text: Given that the order of reactivity of four metals is P>Q>R>S, which of the following reactions is feasible?
36859.explanation: When a metal gives out an electron,it becomes positively charged. The most reactive metal is P, but from the equations given in the options, P should become P+ once it gives out an electron but no option as such. Then we opt for the next most reactive which is Q. If Q gives out an electron, it becomes Q+ while S is the less reactive. Option B is feasible.

36861.subject: Chemistry
36861.question_text: In the electrolysis of CuSO4(aq) using copper electrodes, the reaction at the anode is
36861.explanation:
When copper electrodes are used to electrolyze an aqueous copper sulfate solution, the following happens at the anode:

  • Copper loses electrons: Copper atoms at the anode lose electrons, forming copper ions that go into the solution. 
  • Anode dissolves: The anode slowly dissolves away as the electrolysis continues. 
  • Copper ions are generated: Copper ions are generated at the anode.  In summary, there is dissolution of copper electrode - Option C

36863.subject: Chemistry
36863.question_text: A feasible cell was constructed by joining the two half cells below. Cu\(^{2+}\) (aq) + 2e\(^-\) → Cu(s) E\(^0\) = +0.34 V; Zn\({^2+}\) + 2e\(^-\) → Zn\((_s)\) E\(^0\) = - 0.76V. What is the standard e.m.f. of the cell?
36863.explanation:
The standard e.m.f. of a cell is calculated by subtracting the standard reduction potential of the anode from the standard reduction potential of the cathode:

                       E\(^0\)\(_{cell}\) =  E\(^0\)\(_{cathode}\) - E\(^0\)\(_{anode}\)

 Since   E\(^0\)\(_{Cu^{2+}}\)  >   E\(^0\)\(_{Zn^{2+}}\), it can be inferred that Copper is reduced at the cathode while Zinc is oxidized at the anode.

                       E\(^0\)\(_{cell}\) =  E\(^0\)\(_{Cu^{2+}}\)  -  E\(^0\)\(_{Zn^{2+}}\)

                                              = + 0.34 - (- 0.76)

                                              = + 0.34 + 0.76

                                              = +1.10V

The standard e.m.f. of the cell is +1.10V

36866.subject: Chemistry
36866.question_text: Benzene produces more soot than ethene on burning because benzene
36866.explanation: Benzene has a higher carbon content than other saturated hydrocarbons, like ethene. This invariably means it has a higher molar mass. When benzene burns, it forms elementary carbon, which causes it to burn with a sooty flame. Benzene is a member of the aromatic hydrocarbon family, which are nonpolar molecules that are usually colourless liquids or solids.

is a liquid at room temperature

36871.question_text: One of the products of combustion of pentane in excess air is
36871.explanation: Combustion of Hydrocarbons will usually yield two products: CO2 and H2O. Pentane is an Hydrocarbon, hence one of it's product on combustion will be Carbon(iv)oxide

36873.question_text:
What is the function of H2SO4 in the following reaction?

C12H22O11 conc. H2SO4 → 12C + 11H2O
36873.explanation:
When table sugar (sucrose) is dehydrated with concentrated sulfuric acid (H2SO4), the sugar turns into a column of carbon, and water and carbon dioxide are produced.

This is a dehydration reaction, which is a chemical reaction that removes water from a molecule or ion.

36874.subject: Chemistry
36874.question_text: Which of the following constitutes an advantage in the use of hard water?
36874.explanation: Drinking hard water can help strengthen bones because it contains calcium, an essential mineral for bone health. Your body absorbs calcium from hard water the same way it does from other food sources.

36875.subject: Chemistry
36875.question_text: Sugars can be hydrolyzed at room temperature by the action of
36875.explanation:
Simple sugar molecules (monosaccharide ) when combined to form larger molecules (dissacharides or polysaccharides) is called condensation , water molecules is generated in the process, the reverse process is known as hydrolysis. sugar can be hydrolyszed at room temperature by the action of enzymes.

Sugars can be hydrolyzed by the action of enzymes:

  • Invertase: Hydrolyzes sucrose (table sugar) into glucose and fructose. Yeast normally secretes this enzyme.
  • Lactase: Hydrolyzes lactose in milk. Many adults do not produce lactase and cannot digest lactose.

36878.subject: Chemistry
36878.question_text: If 10 cm 3 of distilled water is added to 10 cm3 of an aqueous salt solution, the concentration of the solution
36878.explanation: The concentration of a solution is the amount of a constituent divided by the total volume of the mixture. When water is added to a solution, the total volume increases, but the number of moles of solute remains the same. This results in a decrease in concentration.

36880.subject: Chemistry
36880.question_text: Which of the following reactions represents the change that occurs when a photographic film is exposed to sunlight?
36880.explanation:
When photographic film is exposed to sunlight, it undergoes a chemical reaction that converts light energy into chemical energy. This reaction causes the film to change chemically and appear black, spoiled, or unable to be developed.The silver bromide in the film breaks down into silver grains. The film produces free silver, which appears as black spots.

The chemical equation for this reaction is:

  • 2 AgBr → 2 Ag  + Br2  Ag gains an electron to become reduced to Ag metal. -Option B

36888.subject: Chemistry
36888.question_text: Acidic industrial waste can be treated with
36888.explanation: Lime is by far the most widely used neutralizing agent for industrial acidic waste waters. Lime, also known as calcium hydroxide, reacts with the acidic components in waste to form water, salts, and other less harmful compounds.

36889.subject: Chemistry
36889.question_text: Waste plastics accumulate in the soil and pollute the environment because plastic materials are
36889.explanation: The bonds between the molecules in plastic are very strong, so microorganisms can't break them down.Thus, they are non-biodegradable.

36893.explanation: Ernest Rutherford's alpha-scattering experiment led to the conclusion that atoms are mostly empty space, with a nucleus that contains the atom's positive charge.

36894.subject: Chemistry
36894.question_text: If a metal R forms a compound with the formula R(NO3)2 the formula of its tetraoxosulphate (VI) is
36894.explanation:
The compound R formed with  R(NO3)2 shows that the metal R has a valency of +2. 

If R reacts with tetraoxosulphate(VI), SO4  2- has a valency of - 2.

If both react or combine together, their valencies will cancel out each other, which implies the formula will be RSO4.

36895.subject: Chemistry
36895.question_text: Which of the following decreases when a given mass of gas is compressed to half its initial volume?
36895.explanation:
Boyle's Law states that the volume of a given mass of gas is inversely proportional to its pressure at a constant temperature. As particles are constantly moving and colliding with each other and the walls of their container. The particles are far apart, so the forces between them are negligible. 

When a gas is compressed, the gas particles move faster and hit the walls of the container more often. This increases the pressure of the gas and invariably brings the molecules of the gases closer together, and this leads to a decrease in the average distance between them.

36901.question_text: A major factor considered in selecting a suitable method for preparing a simple salt is its
36901.explanation:
The major factor to consider when selecting a method for preparing a simple salt is the salt's solubility in water: 

  • Soluble in water: A salt can be prepared by titration. 
  • Insoluble in water: A salt can be prepared by precipitation. In this method, the insoluble salt is precipitated, washed, and dried.

36902.subject: Chemistry
36902.question_text: Which of the following acids forms normal salts only?
36902.explanation: Trioxonitrate(v) acid will only form one type of salt because it is a monobasic acid i.e. it contains only one replaceable hydrogen atom.

36906.subject: Chemistry
36906.question_text: A substance is said to be hygroscopic if it absorbs?
36906.explanation:
Hygroscopy is the phenomenon of attracting and holding water molecules via either absorption or adsorption from the surrounding environment,

which is usually at normal or room temperature.

Deliquescence, the process by which a substance absorbs moisture from the atmosphere until it dissolves in the absorbed water and forms a solution.

moisture from the atmosphere without dissolving

36909.subject: Chemistry
36909.question_text: Which of the following substances increases in mass when heated in air?
36909.explanation:
The mass of magnesium ribbon increases when heated in air because it combines with oxygen to form magnesium oxide, a white powder: 

The chemical equation for this reaction is:

2Mg + O2 → 2MgO

36910.subject: Chemistry
36910.question_text: Calculate the mass of sodium hydroxide in 5.00 dm3 of a 0.125 mol dm-3 solution [NaOH = 40 g mol]
36910.explanation: 1 mole of NaOH per dm3 has a mass of 40g mass of NaOH in 0.125 mole = 0.125 x 40 = 5g mass in 5.00 dm3 of the solution = 5 x 5 = 25.0g

36911.subject: Chemistry
36911.question_text: Which of the following salt solutions will have a pH greater than 7?
36911.explanation: The pH of a solution of sodium carbonate is greater than 7 because it's a basic salt. When Na2CO3 is dissolved in water, it undergoes hydrolysis, which produces OH- ions, making the solution pH greater than 7.

36912.subject: Chemistry

36912.explanation: If more heat is applied to an exothermic reaction in equilibrium, it means temperature is increased, this will however, cause the equilibrium shift to the left. This means the product will decompose to produce more of the reactants on the LHS. i.e XY\(_3\) will decompose.

the forward reaction will go to completion

36913.subject: Chemistry
36913.question_text: Equal amounts of marble chips are reacted separately with 100cm3 of hydrochloric acid of different concentrations . if all the marble chips reacted, which of the following remained the same in each case?
36913.explanation:
When marble chips (calcium carbonate) react with hydrochloric acid, they produce carbon dioxide gas, water, and calcium chloride. The chemical reaction is represented by the equation  CaCO3 + 2HCl → CaCl2 + H2O + CO2. 

The rate of the reaction is proportional to the number of collisions between reactant molecules. Increasing the concentration of hydrochloric acid increases the number of acid particles in the same volume of liquid, which increases the frequency of collisions. If equal amounts of marble chips react separately with different concentrations of hydrochloric acid, the amount of carbon dioxide gas produced remained the same in each case

options.text: Average rate of evolution of gas
Total mass of gas evolved during the reaction
Time taken for the reaction to reach completion

36914.subject: Chemistry
36914.question_text: CuSO4 5H2O can be obtained from an aqueous solution of copper (ll) tetraoxosulphate (VI) by
36914.explanation: Crystallization is the process by which solids form when atoms or molecules are organized into a crystal structure. The resulting crystal's attributes depend on factors like temperature, air pressure, cooling rate, and time of fluid evaporation. copper (II) sulphate pentahydrate (CuSO4⋅5H2O) can be obtained from an aqueous solution of copper (II) tetraoxosulphate (VI) by crystallization.

36915.subject: Chemistry
36915.question_text: Which of the compounds will leave a metal residue when heated?
36915.explanation: AgNO3 is also known as lunar caustic because it: Creates a burning sensation and Leaves a black stain similar to the moon. Silver nitrate (AgNO3) will leave a metal residue when heated strongly.
